To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

US agriculture uses a great deal of P fertilizer, that a large portion of this fertilizer use occurs in export-oriented production, and that the P embodied in US food imports is comparable in size to the P embodied in food exports, with both being larger than the P embodied in the food produced domestically.
US agriculture is highly export oriented and that US food consumption relies heavily on the production of feed and meat in other countries, which in turn rely on large amounts of P fertilizer.
US agricultural systems use large amounts of non-renewable phosphorus resources to feed both domestic and global consumers and that the US is both a net importer and a net exporter of phosphorus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the P fertilizer used to produce US agricultural commodities, and the P fertilizer used for the production of US agricultural commodities that are traded internationally.
the global connections of the US agriculture, which is the world's second largest agricultural producer and consumer of P fertilizer.
the embodied P flows associated with the US agricultural sector and its global connections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the global food system has a large and complex impact on US P fertilizer use and the US food system has an important impact on global P fertilizer use.
the US is not a net P exporter, but rather a net P importer.
the US is a net importer of phosphorus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the US agricultural system is a net exporter of phosphorus, with a large fraction of P inputs to US agriculture being exported with crops or livestock.
the United States is not only a large consumer of food but also a large consumer of phosphorus, and that our food system is a major contributor to the depletion of the world's phosphorus resources.
we have found that US agriculture has a very large P footprint.
The main takeaway from our work is that
US agriculture, in particular its livestock sector, is highly dependent on global P flows.
the US agricultural system is not self-sufficient, nor is it a closed system, but rather it is a part of a global system that includes the US as a major exporter and importer.
the P fertilizer use embodied in the US agricultural trade is large and may be more important than domestic P use in determining the future of the global P cycle.
